summary.intent: Get PR #543 (rollback of lockfiles/manifests after a failed `callisto version` lockfile refresh, E208) past repeated automated review findings, then work out the right architectural fix for the E208-then-E121 recovery problem across current and future ecosystems.
summary.outcome: Rollback was judged the wrong mechanism after four review rounds. Reading ADR 10 and versioning.md showed retain-inputs-and-retry is the intended design, so the recommendation became making interrupted `version` runs resumable by planning from HEAD versions. The read-only fix was committed locally as superseded WIP, and a spike branch off origin/main was created to verify resume assumptions; nothing further was pushed.

repo: ADR 10 (native-resolution-after-version) makes each ecosystem's native tool the oracle for resolution after `version`; a failed lockfile refresh is a coded error (E208) and Callisto does not reimplement resolvers.
Apply refreshes the lockfile and stages before consuming changesets, so a failed refresh deliberately leaves changesets in place as recovery material (versioning.md:27).
Apply is already idempotent per bump via from/to: a manifest at `from` is written, one at `to` counts as done, anything else is refused (versioning.md:25).

E121 (manifest differs from HEAD while release inputs remain, looks like an interrupted run) is the documented limit of recovery, not a bug; E208's help text 'fix it, then re-run' contradicts it by sending users into E121.
Language-specific rules, such as Cargo requiring a dev-dependency range to cover the new version, must not go into the language-agnostic core; they can only be optional hints inside one ecosystem.

New ecosystems need three things for resume: a reader for the effective version at HEAD, a write idempotent by from/to, and a refresh command safe to re-run. Inherited versions (Maven parent, .NET props) go through the existing 'authority' notion, and ecosystems with no manifest version (Go) only repeat refresh and staging.
Dev-dependency range failures are the more common E208 trigger and arise from the new version, so a refresh before versioning would not catch them.

code.finding: Planning takes base versions from `ws.base_versions()`, which reads the on-disk manifests. This is why a re-run after a partial apply bumps again and trips E121.
`manifest_version_at` reads a manifest's effective version at HEAD, including inheritance. E121 already uses it, so it can be reused to plan from HEAD versions when resuming.
Preflight lets a read-only Cargo.toml in a writable directory pass. Atomic replacement then bumps it while preserving its read-only mode, so an in-place restore fails with PermissionDenied.

workflow: When review findings keep arriving on one mechanism, treat that as a sign the mechanism is wrong. State the invariant and enumerate its dimensions before patching, and run the review prompt against your own diff before pushing.
Read the existing ADRs and architecture docs before designing a fix; they showed that several recommended options contradicted decisions already made.
Verify a design with a throwaway spike checked differentially, comparing an interrupted-then-resumed run against a clean run across several workspace shapes, before committing to implementation.
Check CI results by exit code rather than by grepping test output.
Each push triggers a new automated review, so pushing quickly and answering each finding one at a time encourages whack-a-mole fixes.
